patch.value: A hardcoded fixture date aged out of the seven day window and broke the daily release

The metrics fixture pinned a closed item at 2026-08-03. On 2026-08-10 it became 7.27 days old, so no fixture satisfied the seven day throughput comparison, its true branch became unreachable and the coverage gate failed at 99.89 percent with no code change.

value.author: claude
value.text: The blast radius was fleet wide rather than local. pm-ops 2026.8.8 is the pin fifteen repositories use for the canonical docstring analyzer, and the fix that stops it scanning gitignored .agents/pm/extensions artifacts merged as 25b700f after that release. With the daily release failing, no published pm-ops carried that fix, so every adopting repository kept the local versus CI divergence CodeRabbit flagged on pm-csv pull request 65.

value.author: claude
value.text: The tell was that the release succeeded on 2026-08-09 and failed on 2026-08-10 with no commit in between. A gate that changes verdict without an input change is measuring the clock. Here the fixture closed_at was 6.27 days old at the last success and 7.27 days old at the failure.

value.author: claude
value.text: Verified the branch total rather than only the percentage. index.ts reports 911 branches found both before and after, hit 910 then 911, so the missing branch was covered rather than made unreachable. A percentage alone cannot distinguish those two outcomes because V8 omits branches in code it never executes.
